decision: Measured the machine and the clone before designing: 2 vCPU, 3 GB RAM, no SCons, 1.2 GB of git history.
why: A full engine build would take hours and could run out of memory, so verification had to use the official binary.
result: No source build this session.

decision: Merge upstream tags into main behind a thin allowlist. Do not rebase and do not rebrand every file.
why: Merging keeps public history stable and limits 4.8 conflicts to the few files gai edits.
result: Accepted; enforced by bin/gai upstream check.

decision: Kept the Godot project in game/ instead of the repository root.
why: The root holds 14k engine files; a project.godot there would make Godot import the engine source.
result: The editor opens game/ directly.

decision: Chose one Python CLI over an MCP server or an editor panel.
why: Agents already have a shell, and the CLI works in pi, opencode, CI, and a terminal with no extra process.
result: Accepted.

decision: Changed version.py name to gai and the website URL. Kept short_name=godot and the godot binary name.
why: methods.py:268 asserts short_name is godot, and platform/linuxbsd/SCsub:44 hardcodes #bin/godot. Changing them adds build conflicts for no visible gain.
result: The window title and version header read gai.

decision: Check runs three stages: import assets, parse every .gd with --check-only, then run the main scene.
why: Godot 4.7.2 exits 0 on parse and runtime errors, so an exit-code check passes a broken game.
result: Parse error and runtime error both fail check; the clean project passes.

decision: Installed the official engine through bin/gai engine install.
why: This proves the download, SHA-512 check, and extraction with the real release.
result: 139.6 MiB downloaded; version 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf; exit 0.

decision: Tested the upstream tools against a synthetic 4.8 tag with a clean merge, a README conflict, an abort, and an out-of-layer edit.
why: The real 4.8 tag does not exist, so the merge runbook needed a local proof.
result: 5 tests pass.

decision: Push main to git@github.com:jerryshell/gai.git.
why: The target repository was empty and the user asked for it to be the distribution.
result: open

decision: Pushed main to origin at 4ca7679ba3.
why: The empty target repository now holds the full Godot history and the gai layer.
result: ok

decision: Stripped a leading -- from bin/gai run arguments before calling the engine.
why: The documented run -- --headless command reached the engine as --, so the engine ignored --headless and tried to open a display.
result: `run -- --headless --quit-after 2` exits 0 and prints the scene ready line.

decision: Taught the merge command to resolve version.py by taking upstream file and re-applying name and website.
why: A real 4.8 bump conflicts on the adjacent website and docs lines; the brand is two declarative keys, so the resolution is deterministic.
result: 7 tests pass, including a version bump and a version bump plus README conflict.

decision: Independent review found a stale-engine gate hole, a missed SHADER ERROR, a false input rule, and a thin layer guard.
why: The findings were specific and reproduced, so I fixed them before calling 0.1.0 done.
result: 5 fixed; repo visibility is the owner's action.

decision: Made check refuse an engine or version.py that does not match the recorded upstream tag, including two-part tags such as 4.8-stable.
why: The old doctor check silently skipped 4.8-stable, so a forgotten engine install would leave every gate green on the old engine.
result: Stale engine and stale version.py both fail check.

decision: Added SHADER ERROR to the error scan and an end-to-end test that injects a parse error.
why: The scan missed one of Godot's error kinds, and no test proved check can fail.
result: Parse error exits 1; clean project exits 0.

decision: Corrected the input action rule in AGENTS.md and the skill.
why: Godot prints an error for an undeclared action, and check catches it; the old text told agents the gate was blind.
result: Verified with a headless run.

decision: Added a required file list and a clean-tree check before an upstream merge.
why: A deleted core file or a dirty tree could leave the layer check green.
result: 9 tests pass.

decision: Added the version-string update step to the upstream runbook.
why: A 4.8 merge leaves 4.7 strings in the docs and the editor rewrites project.godot.
result: The runbook now greps for the old version.

decision: Extended the layer check to untracked files outside owned paths.
why: A committed diff cannot see a local engine file, and the review showed the check stayed green with one present.
result: 10 tests pass.

decision: Downloaded the official 4.7.2 mono Linux editor and ran a headless Web export on a plain project; it failed with the .NET Web export guard.
why: The feature doc claims the official editor blocks .NET web export, so the claim needed a runtime check, not only the source guard.
result: Failed with "Exporting to Web is currently not supported in Godot 4 when using C#/.NET."

decision: Replaced the thin-layer allowlist with feature-owned divergence. The engine is now a first-class part of gai.
why: The product is AI-native and needs deep engine changes; the thin layer blocked the product.
result: 11 upstream tests pass; check and doctor pass.

decision: Recorded .NET web export as a planned high-risk feature. Upstream 4.7.2 refuses it; the available patch targets 4.8-dev and Windows.
why: The requested feature is allowed by the new architecture but still needs a custom engine build and a base-version decision.
result: Not active; blocked on a build platform.

decision: Chose the engine agent bridge as the first vertical AI-native feature.
why: The CLI cannot see live editor state; an in-engine bridge gives agents scene, input, and screenshot control.
result: Planned; design recorded.

decision: Fixed the planned/active test gap, report path listing, the merged status trap, and the token ignore.
why: The independent review reproduced each issue; the core ownership rule had no test that could fail.
result: 15 upstream tests pass.

decision: Made check tolerate the headless editor shutdown abort after a completed import.
why: The editor can abort at exit with `singleton is null` while the import itself finished; the run step still verifies the assets.
result: 4 check tests pass; check ok.

decision: Implemented the first agent bridge slice: headless runtime JSON-RPC, scene.tree, node.get, node.set, CLI, token auth, and an end-to-end test.
why: The bridge is the first vertical AI-native feature; the engine now exposes live scene state to the agent.
result: Agent test, 15 upstream tests, 4 check tests pass.

decision: Fixed the agent bridge review findings: client replacement and deadlines, PID start-time verification, JSON-RPC errors, start/stop lock, atomic 0600 state, buffered writes, and tests.
why: The review reproduced blocking clients, a foreign PID kill, silent error results, and orphan starts.
result: 3 agent tests pass; check and the other 19 tests pass.

decision: Made bootstrap build the gai engine from source by default; the official Godot binary is now an explicit fallback.
why: The stock binary lacked the gai display name and agent bridge, and its .godot cache could conflict with the source build. The deep fork must run its own engine.
result: bootstrap used the built engine; --official used the fallback; both check ok. The build command is the proven 1:11:23 build.

decision: Exposed the engine reflection to agents: ClassDB/Object handles, singletons, scene/node/resource/project/run/input/screenshot, generic agent call, and editor mode.
why: An AI-native engine must expose all low-level capabilities, not a hand-written subset; reflection makes every engine class and singleton reachable.
result: 5 agent tests pass; 1054 classes and 41 editor singletons reachable.

decision: Made the engine fully editable for game work; upstream check and merge warn by default, and --strict is for gai canonical CI.
why: The agent owns the full source and must be able to change any engine file for a game requirement. Feature records are for upstream maintenance, not permission.
result: 17 upstream tests pass; warning and strict paths both tested.

decision: Fixed the capability review: safe object frees, type-aware string conversion, parseable var_to_str reads, collision-free error results, editor guards, and the engine CI job.
why: The review reproduced an engine crash from freeing a singleton, silent string corruption, unparsable Vector2 reads, error-key collisions, and editor run/scene/input effects.
result: 5 agent tests pass; engine CI job added.

decision: Integrated GodotSteam 4.23.2 as an engine module instead of a GDExtension, with Valve's SDK installed outside git.
why: The module makes Steam a ClassDB singleton in every process, so the agent bridge reaches it with no bridge code; the SDK is not MIT and must not be committed.
result: Module vendored; SDK installer pinned to 1.65.

decision: Vendored GodotSteam with one config.py patch, added `bin/gai steam status|sdk|runtime|vendor`, copied the SDK library next to the engine, and added a CI SDK step.
why: A clone must build without the SDK and enable Steam with one command; the library needs an $ORIGIN runpath, and the module should update from a checkout without hand-copying every file.
result: Build ok; readelf shows RUNPATH [$ORIGIN]; steam sdk --download and --from verified.

decision: Verified Steam through the agent bridge: ClassDB surface, both singletons, registered settings, a failed init without a client, and the runtime library.
why: A built class is only useful if an agent can discover and call it; the failure path must be safe on machines without Steam.
result: 5 Steam tests pass; steamInitEx returns status 1 and a verbal error; agent tests and check still pass.

decision: Added external-project mode: `GAI_GAME` moves the game, runtime state, and check/agent/export paths outside the gai repo.
why: An agent must be able to dogfood gai on a real commercial project without copying that project into the engine repository.
result: External check passes; agent start/tree/stop works; state lives in <game>/.gai.

decision: Replaced per-script `--check-only` with a scene-based script loader when the project has autoloads, and added `check --scene`.
why: `--check-only` cannot resolve autoload names, so a real project produced more than 100 false errors. A scene run has the autoloads; loading every script from it compiles them correctly.
result: External project: 9 autoloads, 78 scripts, check ok with the gameplay scene.

decision: Added `bin/gai export web` with template detection, `--clean`, and `--gzip`.
why: A web export was a manual chain of download, extract, export, and gzip; an agent should get one command.
result: Export produced index.html, index.wasm, index.pck, and .gz files.

decision: Deployed a web build outside the repo and found the GodotSteam GDExtension conflict; the check now names it.
why: The built-in Steam module and the addon both register `Steam`; the engine logged a shutdown error instead of a useful message.
result: Check reports the addon conflict; the web build runs without Steam.

decision: Warm up a fresh project with one import pass, then gate on a second import.
why: A first import can print load-before-import errors or abort at shutdown while it builds the cache; the second pass is the real result.
result: tests/test_check.py passes; a fresh copy of a 78-script project checks ok.

decision: Read ~/jenova as a reference for the four gaps in gai: build time, gate choice, crash visibility, script reflection.
why: Jenova solves the same problems inside an extension with a watchdog, a compiler cache, MSE, and a compile-time reflection pass; gai has the fork and lacks the four outcomes.
result: Four features scoped; no jenova code copied.

decision: Added `bin/gai next`: one ordered glob table, highest gate wins, `--json`, `--run`.
why: A rule table is the whole design; the gate is a maximum over paths, so a mixed change cannot under-test itself.
result: 16 tests pass; `next` on a mixed change prints rebuild-check.

decision: `bin/gai build` runs the compiler through sccache or ccache when one is on PATH, with `--no-cache`.
why: The cold build is the largest cost an agent pays, and a compiler cache is the only change that cannot alter any other SCons flag.
result: 12 tests pass with a fake ccache on PATH.

decision: Added `script.classes` and `script.class` to the bridge, reading the import cache first and a bounded res:// scan second.
why: The global class cache is editor-written, so a game run starts without it; a fresh project must still answer on the first call.
result: Fresh project answers from the scan; second call reports cached true.

decision: Named the crashing call in a record instead of containing the fault.
why: Linux has no structured exception handling, and a longjmp out of a signal handler leaves engine locks held; a named death is honest.
result: SIGSEGV during object.call writes method, target, and signal; clean stop removes the record.

decision: `check` and `lint` write `.gai/logs/diagnostics.json`; both take `--json`, and MCP attaches the record to `gai_check` and to bridge errors.
why: An agent should read one record with path and line instead of a log, and the same parser already backed `lint`.
result: Parser tests pass; a parse error reports res://scripts/main.gd:3; a fresh import still writes ok true.

decision: Replaced the CC="ccache cc" prefix with two wrapper scripts at absolute paths after the real build failed.
why: SCons runs $CC as one program: the first build through the prefix died with `sh: 1: ccache c++: not found` on 2 objects, so a dry-run test alone had proved nothing.
result: test_wrapper_runs_the_cache_and_the_compiler runs the wrapper; 874 compile invocations went through a logging shim; build: ok.

decision: Measured the engine build loop and the cost of a header that many files include.
why: The module object compiles in 5.6 s and a relink after a module change takes 19 to 33 s, so the loop is cheap; display_server_offscreen.h forced 874 recompiles and about 31 minutes in two runs.
result: build: up to date; check: ok with 14 game tests; engine tests 11 agent, 14 check, 19 mcp, 17 upstream, 16 next, 12 build, 3 lint-parser.

decision: Ran every test file in tests/ except the two helper scripts, then pushed a branch and opened pull request 3.
why: A branch plus a pull request is everything that does not need the maintainer; merging does.
result: PR 3: fork, game, and engine jobs all green, including the crash and reflection tests.

decision: `next` now reads git status as (path, status) pairs and sends a deleted game script to the check gate.
why: A deleted script cannot be compiled, so `check --script` failed with a load error instead of checking the scenes that referenced the file.
result: The git-status test commits a script, deletes it, and reads gate check with rule `game/**/*.gd (deleted)`.

decision: Guarded `get_documentation` with TOOLS_ENABLED after the Windows matrix failed on three of four jobs.
why: `Script::get_documentation` is editor-only, so the module compiled for the editor and broke every template build; the local gate never compiled that configuration.
result: One-file template object compiles in 5.1 s; editor build, check, and the agent and check tests pass.

decision: Moved the crash-record state inside the feature guard after clang-cl reported it unused.
why: On Windows the guard is off, so the struct and its instance existed and nothing read them; the Windows editor job treats that warning as an error.
result: Both module objects compile for target=template_release with MinGW in 7.4 s; the Linux editor build, check, and agent tests pass.

decision: `build --check` now answers from a content stamp in `.gai/build/<target>-<host>.json` instead of mtimes.
why: A checkout, a merge, or a formatter pass rewrites the same bytes, and the mtime answer cost three pointless rebuilds in one session.
result: An mtime bump stays up to date; a one-byte edit reads stale and names the file.

decision: `build --objects` compiles one source for a target, and `next` puts a template object compile between build and check.
why: The editor target never compiles without TOOLS_ENABLED, so an editor-only API broke every template build and only CI saw it.
result: Removing the TOOLS_ENABLED guard on purpose fails the object in 2.6 s with the same error CI took 25 minutes to find.

decision: Bridge roles (`read-only`, `write`, `admin`) over one access table, plus `.gai/logs/audit.jsonl` for mutating calls.
why: Pi Pocket is shared; the bridge was a single trusted interface where any token holder could quit the game or rewrite a scene.
result: Read-only refuses node.set and run.quit with -32003, reads pass, ping reports the role, and the audit log holds one line per mutating call.

decision: Moved the role from the process to the token: `agent start` mints one token per role and `--role` on start becomes a ceiling.
why: A client could ask for a lower role only by trusting itself; a token is the one thing a client cannot forge, so the boundary has to sit there.
result: Read-only token refuses node.set and admin-only run.quit, write token refuses run.quit, the process ceiling caps all three, and an unknown token is still -32001.

decision: The audit line names the effect of an `object.call` as `Class.method`, and carries the role and the ceiling.
why: `object.call` hides the real target, so "who ran OS.execute" was unanswerable from a line that only said object.call.
result: An object.call to OS.get_process_id writes effect OS.get_process_id with allowed true.

decision: The build stamp now hashes the content of every dirty engine file.
why: The stamp recorded which files were dirty, not what they held, so a second edit to an already-dirty file read as up to date and the old binary survived a rebuild request.
result: A second edit to a dirty file reads stale; the test builds with a fake scons to write the stamp.

decision: The build stamp keys on a tree hash per engine directory plus the content of every dirty file, not on HEAD or on the status letter.
why: Merging docs-only branches moved HEAD and raised a stale answer, and a second edit to an already-dirty file looked identical to the first.
result: A docs-only commit stays up to date, an engine commit reads stale, and a second edit to one dirty file reads stale.

decision: A request can lower its own ceiling with a `ceiling` field; raising is ignored.
why: A client could hold an admin token and still promise to be harmless, which is the reverse of the process ceiling and costs one comparison.
result: ceiling read-only refuses node.set with "runs as read-only", a bad ceiling is -32602, and the read-only token stays read-only whatever it asks for.

decision: Node locks with a holder name, a TTL, and -32004 for a write inside someone else's lock.
why: Two agents on one scene overwrote each other in silence, and the roadmap's P1 done-when asks for exactly this.
result: A lock on /root/Main blocks agent-b and a guest, allows agent-a including through a handle, and lock.list shows the holder.

decision: Locks belong to a holder name and outlive the connection, not to a connection.
why: `bin/gai agent call` opens one connection per call, so a lock tied to a connection would die before the next command could use it.
result: Acquiring twice with one holder returns the same lock with reused true; a lock survives the call that took it.

decision: `lock.renew`, and any request that carries a holder renews that holder's locks; an admin may release or renew a lock it does not hold.
why: A fixed TTL expires under a long edit, and a claim whose owner died has to be recoverable without a human.
result: A holder request keeps its lock past its TTL, lock.renew reports the new time, a write-token renew is refused, and an admin release works.

decision: MCP carries `--holder` and `--ceiling` on every request through one `bridge_request` builder, and the agent skill gains a lock section.
why: An MCP session that cannot name a holder can never write inside its own lock, and an agent that does not read the skill will not take one.
result: bridge_request includes both fields; 22 MCP tests and 19 agent tests pass.

decision: `stub_once` answers in turn, and a double of a subclass overrides methods its base script declares.
why: The roadmap's own test-maturity leftover: every fixture needed a wrapper script to be stubbable, and a fixed sequence had no way to be tested.
result: 17 game tests pass, including an inherited `take_damage` and a three-call sequence.

decision: CODEOWNERS covers `/game/` and `/tests/*.py` instead of a list of test files.
why: validate-codeowners failed on every game file an agent touches, which is most edits in this repository.
result: validate-codeowners passes for game and test files.

decision: test_lint asserts the shape of the script count, not the number.
why: A new fixture script made a hard-coded "lint: 8 scripts" fail in CI while the lint itself was clean.
result: The assertion is a regex over "lint: <n> scripts, 0 problems"; 11 lint tests pass.

decision: Ran gai against nova-survivors-gai: doctor, check, 35 scene tests, lint, a Linux export, and the new bridge features.
why: The roadmap's dogfood item needs a real project, and it exists on this machine; nothing in a synthetic starter game exercises 15 autoloads, 94 class_names, or a 190 MiB export.
result: check ok, 35 scene tests pass, lint 147 scripts 0 problems, export 190.4 MiB starts headless, script.classes returns 94 classes, locks and audit behave on the real scene.

decision: `next` maps a path inside an external project to the script, test, and check gates, instead of sending every script edit to the full check.
why: Dogfooding found it: with GAI_GAME set, `components/x.gd` matched only the catch-all rule, so the cheap gate never applied to a real project.
result: An external project .gd gives gate script with res://components/ability.gd and check --script runs in 7.9 s on the real project.
